_readme: NOTES. Finishing the first container in a room leaves a 📝 on the floor.
Pick it up and someone has written to you.
This is deliberately the cheapest possible NPC: no portrait, no dialogue
tree, no voice acting. A handwritten card delivers most of the presence a
character would, establishes a voice, and doesn't interrupt the quiet loop
the game is actually good at. If the writing lands, THEN consider giving
the voice a face.
Keyed by room id. `need` is a list of emoji that must all be filed in
their home container to complete it. If a room has no entry here — or the
listed emoji aren't in this run — a fallback note is generated from
whatever the room actually contains, so every room gets one for free.
`text` is the note. `reply` is what arrives when you finish it.
Keep them to one or two sentences and in the same hand throughout.
A NOTE IS THE ROOM'S VOICE, NOT THE CLIENT'S. That distinction did not
matter while every room was in a house and every house had one kind of
person in it. It matters now: a frat room can turn up in free play, where
nobody hired you and the signature is '— M'. So these are written in the
room's own hand — dry, sentence case, whoever is standing in it — and the
client's voice goes in `note` on their stage in clients.json, which
overrides this. Zorb's ship and Nettle's tower are the two places that bend
the rule, because those rooms belong to one person so completely that a
neutral note would read as nobody at all.
`need` may name emoji a given run does not contain — a level's `types` cap
means a container often takes a slice of its list. That is handled: the
fallback fires and the room still leaves a note.
_signatureNote: The hand a house writes in when nobody hired you — free play, where there
is no client. A campaign note is signed by whoever gave you the job, and
a stage in clients.json can write the whole note itself; everything below
_roomShareNote: roomShare — what fraction of a house's rooms start with a SEALED container.
It was effectively 1.0 (every room), which made a locked cupboard the
resting state of the house instead of an event. 0 turns seals off entirely;
a level or size entry can override it with a `quests` number (a fraction,
or a room count if above 1) or `quests: false`.
Rooms without a seal still leave a note — see `fallback` below.
_sealedNote: Used when the note is about the room's SEALED container — the one that
stays shut until you finish something else in the room. This is the
normal case; `fallback` only fires in rooms with no sealed container.

sealed.text: You got the rest of it done, so here's the key bit: the {container} still needs filling.
sealed.reply: The {container} too. That's the whole room, then. Thank you.

fallback.text: Whoever's tidying: if you get the {container} sorted I'll owe you one.
fallback.reply: The {container}. You actually did it. Thank you.

kitchen.text: Milk, eggs, butter — in the fridge before dinner, please. I keep finding them on the counter.
kitchen.reply: Fridge stocked. Dinner is saved. You're a marvel.

garage.text: The wrench, the hammer, the screwdriver. Back on the bench where they live. I've been looking for that hammer since March.
garage.reply: There it is. Since March. Thank you.

bathroom.text: Pills and plasters in the cabinet, before someone needs them in a hurry.
bathroom.reply: Cabinet sorted. Nobody's bleeding. Good day.

office.text: The document, the receipt, the folder. Filing cabinet. I have an appointment on Thursday and I need to find all three.

bedroom.text: Socks, shirt, jeans — in the dresser. I'd like to get dressed tomorrow without an expedition.
bedroom.reply: Dresser done. Tomorrow will be easy.

closet.text: Suitcase and boots on the travel shelf. I'm not saying we're going anywhere. I'm saying we could.
closet.reply: Packed and ready. We could, you know.

attic.text: The picture and the clock, into the memory chest. Careful with the picture.
attic.reply: Both safe. That picture is older than this house.

shed.text: Seedling and the potted one, on the potting bench where they get light.
shed.reply: They'll take now. Give them a month.

secret.text: You found this room, then. The gem and the crown go in the chest. Don't ask.
secret.reply: Locked away again. We never had this conversation.

playroom.text: The puzzle and the kite, in the toy chest. There are eleven hundred pieces and I have found four of them with my feet.
playroom.reply: Toy chest shut. My feet thank you personally.

music.text: Microphone and headphones back on the sound shelf. Nobody in this house has been quiet since we bought that microphone.
music.reply: Sound shelf sorted. Blessed, blessed silence.

mudroom.text: Skateboard and skates on the gear rack, not in the doorway. I have views about this that you have heard before.
mudroom.reply: Gear rack loaded. Nobody breaks an ankle tonight.

cellar.text: The wine glass and the good bottle, on the rack. The bottle is for an occasion. This is not the occasion.
cellar.reply: Back on the rack. One day, the occasion. Not today.

observatory.text: Telescope and compass into the optics case before the damp gets at the lenses. Clear sky on Thursday.
observatory.reply: Both cased. Thursday, then — bring a coat, it's cold up here.

pong.text: The cups. All of them, on the tower. Whatever else you do, do not knock over the tower.
pong.reply: Cups filed and the tower is still standing. That is the whole of anyone's ambition for this room.

pit.text: Somebody's phone and somebody's headphones are inside this couch. They have been inside this couch since Sunday.
pit.reply: Both recovered. Two people are going to be extremely relieved and neither of them will say so.

laundry.text: A shirt and a pair of socks onto the clean-ish pile. Clean-ish is a real category and this is where it lives.
laundry.reply: Clean-ish restocked. Nobody has to make a decision tomorrow morning.

trophy.text: The trophy and the medal, back in the case. We won those. We definitely won those.
trophy.reply: Behind glass where they can be pointed at. That is what they are for.

kitchenette.text: The plate and the pan. In the sink is not the same as done, but it is a great deal closer than the floor.
kitchenette.reply: Sink loaded, floor clear. This is now technically a kitchen.

study.text: The books back on the shelf. Nobody has opened them. That is not the point.
study.reply: Shelved, spines out. The room looks like studying happens in it, which is exactly the point.

yard.text: The frisbee and the ball off the grass and into the lawn crate, before the mower finds them again.
yard.reply: Both crated. The mower lives to see another Saturday.

rooms._ship: Zorb's survey vessel. These are in his hand; the ship is his and a neutral note would read as nobody.

specimen.text: The specimen and the shell are to be returned to their cases. They are not the same kind of thing. One of them is still alive.
specimen.reply: Both cased. Only one of them minded.

cryo.text: Ice to the frozen stock, gauge to the wall. If you get this the wrong way round I will know within the hour.
cryo.reply: Correct on both counts. The rack is holding at temperature. Thank you.

replica.text: The sitting apparatus and the comfort object. I have watched four hundred hours of your species and I remain unsure which is which.
replica.reply: Filed as you filed them. I have amended the diagram. The diagram was wrong.

instrument.text: Dish and scope into the array. Nothing is currently pointed at anything, which is how a survey becomes four hundred pages of nonsense.
instrument.reply: Array restored. I am once again looking at the correct sky.

anomaly.text: The horse and the eye. The horse is unexplained. The eye I have grown fond of. Do not ask me to justify the difference.
anomaly.reply: Both away, in their correct and entirely arbitrary places. I feel better and I do not know why.

hydro.text: Seedling to the growing beds, carrot to the harvest bin. One of these has a future and one of these is dinner.
hydro.reply: Beds and bin, correctly. Dinner is on schedule. So is the future.

rooms._tower: Nettle's tower, in Nettle's hand, for the same reason as the ship.

library.text: Scroll to the scroll case, book to the shelf. If the scroll starts talking, ignore it.
library.reply: Both away, and it did start talking. You did well to ignore it.

apothecary.text: Test tube to the reagent shelf, herb to the dried rack. What you brew WITH and what you brewed it FROM do not share a shelf.
apothecary.reply: Reagents and herbs, apart, as they should have been these four hundred years.

roost.text: Feather on the rail, owl in the roost. The owl will make this difficult. The owl makes everything difficult.
roost.reply: Both settled. The owl has forgiven you, which it has never once done for me.

scrying.text: The ball and the candle. Nothing in here works without both, and neither works on the floor.
scrying.reply: Set. I can see next Tuesday again and I am sorry to report it looks much like this one.

broom.text: Broom and wand on the same rack. Yes, the same rack. They are both sticks that do a job and I am too old to keep them apart.
broom.reply: One rack, two sticks, no argument. That is how it has always been done.

reliquary.text: Urn to the relics, skull to the cursed shelf. Get that the wrong way round and we will both learn why the shelf is called that.
reliquary.reply: Correct, and nothing happened, which is the finest available outcome in this room.

rooms._zoo: The zoo. Back to the room's own neutral hand — two people run this place and neither owns it.

aviary.text: Feather on the perch rail, nest box back on its bracket. They come apart every time somebody lands badly.
aviary.reply: Rail and bracket, both. The residents already have their claws on it.

keeper.text: The clipboard and the torch. Neither belongs on the floor, and one of them has the feeding times on it.
keeper.reply: Both back on their hooks. Feeding times are legible again, which matters more than it sounds.

feedstore.text: Greens to the produce bins, grain to the dry sacks. Wet and dry — that is the entire filing system down here.
feedstore.reply: Wet with wet, dry with dry. Nothing is going off before Thursday.

reptile.text: Snake to the warm rocks, frog to the damp corner. Warm or damp. Nobody has ever needed a third option.
reptile.reply: Warm and damp, correctly assigned. Everyone in here is as happy as their species allows.

enclosure.text: Toy to the enrichment crate, basket to the bedding store. He will have both back out within the hour. Do it anyway.
enclosure.reply: Both away, and he has already started on the toy. That is a compliment.

vault.text: Bananas in the vault. Only bananas in the vault. This is written on the door and it has not helped.
vault.reply: Bananas in the vault. Nothing else in the vault. I would like that read aloud at the next meeting.
